title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes - Nature Sustainability
byline: Kang; Seongmin; Park; Sung-O; Jang; Ho-Young; Kim; Youngsin; Hyuk-Joon; Ahn; Hongjin; Yu; Seungju; Pant; Bhargavi; Po-Hua; Jonghun; Ko; Kun-Hee; Jeon; Youngjun;
html:
Abstract

Developing sustainable lithium-ion battery cathode materials with high energy density and structural stability is critical for the global clean energy transition. Oxygen-redox chemistry in lithium-rich layered oxides offers additional capacity, but irreversible structural changes cause progressive voltage decay. Here we report a family of lithium-rich layered cathodes, Lix(Li0.15Ni0.20Mn0.65)O2, with a unique O6-type stacking sequence formed by atomic-scale intergrowth of O3- and O1-type subunit cells, and reveal how this architecture regulates oxygen-redox activity and structural reversibility. Combining first-principles calculations with structural and spectroscopic analyses, we show that this intergrown architecture suppresses destructive structural evolution responsible for oxygen-redox degradation, including transition-metal migration and irreversible oxygen dimerization. By preserving the local oxygen coordination environment during cycling, the O6 framework stabilizes oxygen-redox activity and mitigates the associated voltage decay. Consequently, the O6-type cathode exhibits negligible voltage decay and superior energy density retention. Our findings establish atomic-scale stacking as a key design parameter for controlling structural dynamics and oxygen-redox reversibility, providing a general strategy for developing durable, high-energy-density cathodes for next-generation green batteries.
